objective: Close all seven daily-use gaps requested in the supplied task text, retaining the implementation ledger's broader scope and honest verification limits.
completion_rule: Every requirement needs source-specific implementation and applicable executed evidence. Fixtures do not prove physical hardware or third-party compatibility. An unmet target or unavailable required acceptance remains open.

acceptance: An explicitly activated saved personal Wi-Fi profile can request fresh credentials through the native masked prompt.
The existing profile UUID is retained and no duplicate profile is created.
Credentials remain zeroizing, absent from ordinary scenes, inspection, logs and process arguments.
Cancellation, stale answers, profile retirement and daemon replacement revoke prompt authority.
Owned protocol/client cases and native saved-profile recovery demonstrate success, denial and cancellation while preserving unrelated connections.

evidence.scope: Fourteen actual NetworkManager/native GUI checks using owned simulated WPA2 and hidden radios; saved UUID retained, secret repair/cancel/reconnect and exact restoration. This is not physical-radio/enterprise-Wi-Fi acceptance.
All six final checks succeeded; normal protected-main merge.
Automatic documentation deployment succeeded after the merge; this adds no runtime proof.

acceptance: A native token-styled panel edits observed output modes, resolution, refresh, scale and layout through checked domain values and an injected adapter.
Apply captures and validates the exact baseline, keeps at least one usable output and exposes Keep and Revert.
Timeout, explicit Revert, cancellation and client failure restore the captured layout independently of the UI process.
Keep persists only the accepted user-level configuration while preserving unrelated configuration; failed persistence retains recovery.
Owned tests and native panel interaction verify Keep, Revert, timeout and failure recovery with exact final restoration.
Measure identified current binaries with reproducible static and animated desktop workloads, output/source details and bounded restoration.
Meet the accepted normal-desktop 300 MiB process RSS target without reducing design density, effects or content quality.
Measure cold and warm launcher/panel transitions and sustained wallpaper pacing; target 60 FPS on a 60 Hz display for suitable video and follow other source rates.
Distinguish submission timing from presentation/scanout, CPU image payloads, driver allocations and total process RSS.
Settled unrelated surfaces and paused/hidden wallpapers do not repaint continuously; memory and decoder lifetimes remain bounded.
Execute native hardware-GPU acceptance where available and retain any unmet targets explicitly.
Complex scripts shape into positioned glyphs with source clusters, ligatures and deterministic font fallback.
Bidirectional text shares visual order, source mapping, caret, selection, pointer hits and multiline geometry with rendering.
Ordinary fields support native IME preedit, commit, surrounding-text deletion, cursor rectangles and focus retirement.
Masked authentication/credential fields never expose secret surrounding text or preedit through ordinary input state.
ASCII and 1x/2x rendering quality remain covered; mixed-script controls and a real input-method flow have executed acceptance.
Fresh compositor activation tokens are requested for actual user launch intent and delivered to command, D-Bus Activate/Open and declared-action dispatch without stale ambient reuse.
Typed explicit file/URI opening uses captured current application authority, bounded inputs, literal argument arrays and conservative uncertain-reply fallback.
Desktop-entry field codes preserve file/URI semantics, quoting and resource limits; unsupported or invalid combinations fail explicitly.
Application observation includes relevant executable and icon changes without periodic idle rescans or unbounded watches.
Owned protocol tests and native real-application launch/open/activation demonstrate the implemented integration.

evidence.scope: Local strict all-target Clippy and full workspace:800 Rust passed/76 ignored. Native activation/Open/action transport and real kernel observer regressions passed; graphical real-application acceptance remains pending.
Combined application integration and tested Wi-Fi source passed remote checks, including Vulkan visual checks. This is not a graphical activation/file-opening run.

acceptance: Exercise simultaneous native output input/layout, hotplug and output recreation, integer/fractional density and suspend/resume with preserved preferences.
Exercise physical Bluetooth pairing/control and audio device/microphone/routing with explicit device authority and restored configuration.
Exercise actual third-party StatusNotifier/DBusMenu applications and ordinary application clipboard transfers, not only synthetic protocol peers.
Record runtime/source/hardware identities, actual checks and exact restoration; unavailable hardware is an open acceptance item.
Reconcile library and desktop guides, ownership map, skills and implementation ledger against latest source-specific evidence.
Remove stale native-pending claims only where later evidence proves that same behavior; retain broader hardware, interoperability and security limits.
Document new ports/adapters, initialization, registration, client flow, configuration, rollback and measured performance.
Pass Astro checks, root and Pages builds/link validation; keep local LAN docs running and publish through protected-main merge CI.

invariants: Domain contracts are ports; supplied implementations are adapters; production selection belongs in composition roots.
Views and rendering perform no OS operations; appearance uses generated semantic/component design tokens.
Preserve user wallpapers, settings, unrelated connections, packaged Omarchy files and secure session recovery.
One bounded heavy host job at a time; deploy with rollback and stable readiness checks.
Commit and push working milestones; merge protected-main PRs only after exact final revision checks pass.
Accessibility remains deferred by the user; text shaping and IME remain in scope.
